hook: Electrons can act as catalysts that speed up the self-assembly of donor-acceptor complexes.
hook_turn: speed up the self-assembly of donor-acceptor complexes.
summary: Catalysis normally speeds covalent bond formation. Here a small number of electrons, supplied by electricity, light, or mechanical force, repeatedly speed up the assembly of a donor-acceptor complex, giving near-quantitative yields even in open air. The demonstration covers one type of complex, so generality across other assemblies is still to be shown.
title: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
